newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF minister says will take strict steps on Nomura.
newsitem.headline: MOF minister says will take strict steps on Nomura.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Wednesday reiterated that the ministry will take strict measures against Nomura Securities Co Ltd after Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) makes recommendations on possible punishment.
He told a news conference it was regrettable that three former executives of Nomura were arrested on Wednesday by Japanese prosecutors.
Government sources said complaints by the SESC allege that Nomura and the employees made illegal payments to a corporate client totalling 49.7 million yen ($417,600).
On Tuesday, the SESC filed complaints with prosecutors in the Nomura case, asking for criminal charges against three former executives as well as the firm itself.

Since the case became public in March, when the company said that two directors had improperly reimbursed a client for investment losses, Mitsuzuka has said the ministry will take strict measures against Nomura.
Commenting on the arrest, Mitsuzuka said the ministry will keep a close watch on investigations by the SESC. "It is a very serious problem," he said.
